subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit Browser file-injection mode for custom uploaders, and if so should that mode be DataTransfer drop, clipboard paste, native CDP drag, or a narrower named API?
rationale: The requested behavior would deliver managed local files through page-controlled handlers instead of the standard file-input boundary, so automation should not choose a silent fallback without maintainer-approved security semantics and live proof.

options.title: Add explicit drop-file mode
options.body: Create a named Browser upload mode that validates managed paths, targets a caller-specified drop zone, documents security semantics, and proves a ByteUploader-style page live.

options.title: Keep standard upload only
options.body: Leave Browser upload limited to file chooser, direct file input, and Chrome MCP `upload_file`, and document that custom uploaders need site-specific scripts or plugins.

options.title: Prototype behind review
options.body: Allow an experimental API discussion or PR, but do not queue autonomous implementation until the security and live proof requirements are settled.

recommendation.title: Add explicit drop-file mode
recommendation.body: Create a named Browser upload mode that validates managed paths, targets a caller-specified drop zone, documents security semantics, and proves a ByteUploader-style page live.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest Browser upload and adjacent chooser-fix history in the relevant files.
